SOIL-LANG.ORG

A substrate for tools that explain themselves.

Soil is a small homoiconic Lisp with WIT capabilities. It keeps the Lisp bargain — code as data, macros, a live system — and adds typed host interfaces, GPU-resident views, and spores that travel.

In the Lisp family. lisp-lang.org · MIT OR Apache-2.0 · Rust core · native and WASM hosts

WHY SOIL

Small core. Sharp edges. No hidden layers.

The substrate is deliberately thin. The interesting decisions live in the forms and the host boundary, not in a framework between them.

  1. 01

    Homoiconic

    The source, the AST, the docs, and the UI are the same tree. A tool can read and rewrite itself without a second representation.

  2. 02

    Editable

    Every form carries a source span. An agent can replace one form and keep the comments, layout, and everything it did not touch.

  3. 03

    Portable

    One WIT contract, two hosts. The same Lisp runs natively and in the browser; the GPU stays an optional capability, not a requirement.

  1. 01

    Lisp, kept intact

    Homoiconic forms, macros, a small core, and a REPL-shaped workflow. The source, the docs, and the UI do not fork into separate representations.

  2. 02

    GPU when it matters

    Canvas and GPU-resident scenes are a host capability. Trees, forms, and docs stay ordinary HTML/CSS; waveforms and schematics stay on the GPU.

  3. 03

    Boundaries and distance

    WIT makes capabilities typed and portable. Spores are content-addressed, so the same artifact can run on this machine or another host.

LISP, EXTENDED

The Lisp bargain, with a modern substrate.

Lisp gave us code as data, macros, and a live system. Soil keeps that bargain and adds a typed capability boundary, GPU-resident views, and spores that travel between machines.

LEARN

From a form to a running tool.

Start with the language, then the host, then a spore. You do not need a framework to put a real interface on screen.

  1. 01
    Read the roadmap

    Phases from the core language to self-hosting, with done criteria.

  2. 02
    Run an example

    Counter, TODO, calculator, tic-tac-toe. All of them are plain .soil.

  3. 03
    Write a spore

    One manifest and one entry form. A library and an app are the same artifact.

;; tend build
;; tend run

(defun view (state)
  (el "main" (list (attr :class "app"))
    (list
      (el "h1" nil (list (txt "Hello from Soil")))
      (el "p" nil (list (txt "This is a form, not a template."))))))

SPORES

Libraries and apps are the same artifact.

Load it for its functions

A spore that exports forms is a library. Require it, call its functions, compose its views.

Launch it for its entry point

The same spore with a start form is an app. tend resolves it, builds it, and runs it here or on another host.

COMMUNITY

Grow it with us.

Soil is free software. The core is small on purpose. Bring a spore, a capability, or a hard question about what a tool should be able to explain.
